---
title: "Level-offs in climb and descent"
description: "How OPDI finds periods of level flight below the cruise, during the climb and the descent (level-off-climb-start/end, level-off-descent-start/end)."
---

## In one sentence

A level-off is a period of level flight during the climb or the descent,
below the cruise, published as a pair of events at its start and end.

## What it needs

- The geometric level segments of the track (see
  [Level segments](level-segments.qmd#pru-level-segments)).
- A `top-of-climb` and a `top-of-descent` on the track (see
  [Top of climb and top of descent](tops.qmd)).
- The departure and destination airports and their elevations.

## How it is computed

1. A level segment is a **climb level-off** when all of these hold:
   - it ends before the top of climb;
   - its altitude is at least 3,000 ft above the departure airport;
   - it starts within 200 NM of the departure airport;
   - it is not cruise: it is not both at or above 90% of the altitude of the
     top of climb and longer than 300 s.
2. A level segment is a **descent level-off** under the mirror conditions: it
   starts after the top of descent, its altitude is at least 1,800 ft above
   the destination airport (lower than in the climb, because an aircraft on
   final approach is close to level), it ends within 200 NM of the
   destination airport, and it is not cruise.
3. Each level-off gives a start event and an end event, with the altitude of
   the segment. Each takes the position of the report with a position nearest
   in time to it, within 60 s.

## Based on

The definition of level flight and the cruise exclusion box follow the
vertical flight efficiency method of the EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit
(PRU). The level-offs are those counted by ICAO's vertical efficiency
indicators KPI17 (level-off during climb) and KPI19 (level-off during
descent), written in `info.kpi`.

## What is published

Event types `level-off-climb-start`, `level-off-climb-end`,
`level-off-descent-start` and `level-off-descent-end`, with position, altitude,
`distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`. Their `info` holds `kpi`,
`duration_s`, `distance_nm` and `level_ft` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Time flown level in the descent** per arrival airport, the measure behind
  continuous descent operations (CDO) indicators.
- **Level-offs in the climb** per departure airport and runway, for
  continuous climb operations (CCO).
- **Where level-offs happen**: the altitudes (`info.level_ft`) and positions
  that come back most often around an airport.

## Limitations

A flight without both tops has no level-off, and the cruise of light aircraft
splits into many level-offs. See
[Limitations: vertical profile](../limitations.qmd#lim-vertical).
